label: Cage uses records as an instrument
detail: John Cage's Imaginary Landscape No. 1 uses records switched between speeds.

label: 45/45 becomes the US stereo standard
detail: The Record Industry Association of America adopts the Westrex 45/45 stereo disc system as the American standard.

label: IEC 98 published
detail: The IEC disc recording standard that includes the RIAA curve is first published.

label: RCA record-wear study
detail: Woodward and colleagues at RCA publish an electron-microscope study of groove wear in JAES.

label: Technics SL-1200 launched
detail: Matsushita launches the direct-drive SL-1200 under the Technics brand.

label: Scratching discovered (dates disputed)
detail: KEXP dates Grand Wizzard Theodore's discovery of scratching to 1975; other sources say 1977, the early 1980s or the early 1970s.

label: SL-1200MK2
detail: Technics releases the MK2, which it bills as the first turntable developed for discos.

label: DMC championships begin
detail: The DMC World DJ Championships start.

label: 'Turntablism' coined
detail: DJ Babu of the Beat Junkies coins the word turntablism.

label: Final Scratch released
detail: Stanton's Final Scratch, the first DVS software sold to the public, comes out late in the year.

label: Serato Scratch Live
detail: Serato Scratch Live is released with Rane.

label: SL-1200 discontinued
detail: Panasonic announces the end of Technics analog turntables.

label: DMC allows DVS
detail: The DMC championships begin permitting vinyl-emulation systems.

label: SL-1200 returns
detail: The SL-1200G and limited SL-1200GAE are announced at CES and ship in April and October.
